## India: Regulatory Updates & Implementation

India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) 2023 is now fully active, following the finalization and activation of its 2025 Rules. This marks a significant shift in the country's data privacy landscape, with the new framework revolutionizing enforcement mechanisms.
([Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuwFBVV95cUxQdHdLdVFjdzNOd2JqQWxMUEJ2aS1kMEV5Ylp4TllRNFh0dmRqb1laREhLMlQzLUJWNGlBaS1GRDhEelJEeU9VMlJFS0o1ald2aHFIaDVYMEZXaHlBYUN6VHJ4N3lLd09NdFJRZ0s3Um5zQjdJQl9LaXM0N0NFak5JZmVLdS1TWkY1dnpOTV9yMG9JUFZlRGlHQkJnM3E0NmxnaUxZbEg2NmVkVjZKY2luYThubXJSX0t5bDA4), [Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipwFBVV95cUxPV3E3NllEY1dNWGF1R3ZRdExCSVdhWUhneEkyZ1dQQ0h1dm4zUi1Ed3NTQmdvVjRqR2NfbzBzLU14ZUZJUHQyUGhBSG02RVlQcUNaVnJ0YUt0bEY5WE5PNjlLR24xbW5lXzBmNFRzMFhGVUh5UU5Mdk1WVXJSeW1MMDItVXI2UWNlaEhUVjQ5TnVxOFJPUmR3MVFjUlVBUGJELW9zR1ZYNA), [Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiekFVX3lxTFA0MUhxR2JRbkZEUG81Smp1Uy02Z0xtdWZYSnlyLVJVSHQ2eWtleENVY2Iya2tVTUNveFE5Mm1FLUVwd01icDNwT0pqcFZyOGJVNmZSRGJoSjJUT21BOWxkOXFqTmhVRmNSVW5jSGFyQkVlblRoR2FTX01R))

MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan reiterated that there would be no extensions for startups to comply with the DPDPA, emphasizing the immediate need for adherence to the new data protection standards. This firm stance signals the government's commitment to swift and comprehensive implementation.
([Source](https://news.google.))

MeitY informed Parliament that Common Service Centre (CSC) operators are prohibited from storing Aadhaar or banking data, reinforcing specific restrictions on sensitive personal information. This directive highlights the government's focus on protecting critical citizen data handled by public service points.
([Source](https://news.google.))

## India: Compliance Challenges & Sectoral Impact

The DPDPA presents a significant compliance test for various government ministries and state entities, requiring them to overhaul their data processing practices. Experts note that the government itself faces a sweeping challenge in adapting to the new law's requirements.
([Source](https://news.google.))

The DPDPA's impact extends to specific sectors, with discussions focusing on governing learner data risks in EdTech and the implications for Med-Tech, particularly concerning connected healthcare devices. Additionally, the Act's requirements intersect with existing RBI and SEBI mandates, creating a complex compliance landscape for the digital Indian workforce.
